lines.text: Grand Measurer Vance walked out of the dark as if he had come down for a cup of tea. Caddoc and his Hounds spread out behind him.
The drains. Of course it was the drains. You do love your waterworks.
Can I shoot him?
Please.
Wren drew and loosed in one movement, faster than I could see. Vance looked at her.
That was all. He looked at her. And her arrow fell out of the air, and Wren froze where she stood, her bow still raised.
I felt it in my chest. Her thread, going stiff and white, like a rope left out in a blizzard.
A Veil sees threads, Lucan. That's all a Measurer really is. Someone who sees. And at six rings, a Veil can hold what it sees quite still.
He looked at Oswin, and Oswin's sword stopped halfway up. He looked at Tamsin. He looked at Ash in the middle of his leap, and Ash hung there, snarling, frozen, a hand's width from his throat.
One by one, I felt them go numb. Like fingers in the snow. Every thread I had down there, turning to ice.
When he looked at Nell, he frowned, just for a moment, as if a sum had come out wrong. Then he looked away.
Ilse. Do sit down. You haven't anything left that I want.
Then he turned to the cage, and the woman inside it, and his voice went soft. Almost fond.
Do you know how many rings have been grown from her? Two hundred lords, Lucan. Your brother's draught. The Stone that tried to empty you.
Everything you are, I've already harvested from her.
You fix aqueducts. So do I. Springs flood, and drown whole kingdoms. So I build cisterns. I simply decide where the water goes.
And now I have two springs.
He smiled at me, kindly. And I understood that he meant to put me in that cage beside her, and that he had always meant to.
Nobody was watching Ilse. She had begun to climb the gallery stair, with one of Tobin's lanterns in her hand.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and seven, coming soon.
